Average annual per dwelling unit percentage site energy savings by climate ASHRAE 2004 climate zone for applicable dwelling units only In general, climate zones 4–7 experience a higher percentage of energy savings than other climate zones. This is expected given the significant reduction in heating energy shown in the end use breakdown. Climate zones 4A, 5A, 6B, and 7A show greater percentage energy savings than the dwelling units in their respective climate zones. For example, climate zone 4A shows greater savings than 4B and 4C because the average baseline dwelling unit energy consumption in 4A is higher than in the other zones, as shown in Figure 10. This is because climate zone 4A is a more extreme climate than climate zones 4B and 4C. Climate zone 7B shows a larger site energy percentage savings than climate zones 7AK and 8AK because climate zone 7B’s results are driven by natural gas heating savings, which are on average more than three times as large as climate zones 7AK and 8AK savings. In addition, climate zone 7AK shows heat pump fan and cooling electricity increasing after the upgrade. These end use increases further add to the difference in total site energy savings experienced between climate zones 7AK and 7B. The difference among the climate zones savings are also influenced by the electricity consumption from the heat pump heating backup. Climate zone 7B shows a 38% savings on average for this end use, while climate zone 7AK only shows a 23% site energy savings, and this end use is not applicable for climate zone 8AK. This is another reason for the large difference in site energy savings between the three climate zones. 20 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 10. Average site energy consumption for applicable dwelling units only by ASHRAE climate zone Energy consumption is only one way to display impact. On average, unmet heating and cooling hours also decrease. In the baseline, the average applicable dwelling unit had 130 unmet cooling hours and 22 unmet heating hours. After applying advanced air sealing with drill-and-fill wall insulation, these values decrease to 81 and 17, representing reductions of 46% and 27%, respectively. 4.2.2 Aggregated Power Time Series in Select States During the Peak Day Colorado was analyzed for the time-series results.
